## Your surface

`.codex/` is rendered in **pointer** mode: each file names its canonical body under `agentic/` and restates none of it, so what you read there is an address and never the policy itself. Act on the canonical body, not on the pointer.

## What that means when you work here

- `AGENTS.md` at the repository root is read automatically and is the authority here, so this surface deliberately adds no second contract.
- Workflows land under `.codex/automations/`, not `workflows/` — the same canonical bodies as every other surface, under the name this tool uses. A workflow missing from `agentic/workflows/` is missing here too; the reverse cannot happen, because an orphan is deleted on the next render.
- `.codex/mcp.example.json` is the committed example. The live `.codex/mcp.json` is adopter-owned, gitignored, and never rendered by the generator.

## MCP

- Config path for this surface: `.codex/mcp.json` — never committed.
- Committed example: `.codex/mcp.example.json`
- Servers this surface may not install without an explicit human decision: `docker`, `github`, `kubectl`, `postgres`, `prometheus`, `terraform`.
- Nothing is installed automatically. `agentic/mcp_registry.yaml` declares each server's ceiling risk mode, and adding one is a supply-chain decision made on the repository's behalf.

## The mode contract

Every operation carries AUTO, CONSULT or STOP — the three are defined in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#auto-consult-stop) and mapped operation by
operation in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#agent-behavior-protocol). The mode is a
property of the operation, not of the tool running it and not of your
confidence in it: the same procedure carries the same mode here as on every
other surface, and a surface that appears to weaken one has drifted.
